basic_information.name: Dify
basic_information.creator: LangGenius Inc. (co-founded by Luyu Zhang and John Wang in 2023, both former Tencent engineers). Headquarters in Middletown, Delaware (USA) with R&D center in Suzhou, China. ~70 employees as of mid-2025.
basic_information.description: Dify is an open-source AI application development platform that combines a visual workflow builder, built-in RAG knowledge base engine, agent framework, and LLMOps capabilities into a unified low-code/no-code environment. It serves as a Backend-as-a-Service (BaaS) for building production-ready AI applications. Dify stands out for its intuitive drag-and-drop workflow studio, broad LLM provider support (OpenAI, Anthropic, Google, Mistral, open-source models), and its Knowledge Pipeline feature for enterprise-grade RAG. With 127K-129K GitHub stars, it is one of the most popular open-source AI platforms globally, serving 120+ countries including 30+ Fortune 500 companies. The platform removed LangChain from its codebase to build a more streamlined set of components, and introduced a plugin ecosystem with Marketplace in v1.0 (February 2025).
basic_information.release_date: Initial open-source release in 2023; v1.0.0 released February 2025 (plugin architecture milestone); latest versions v1.11.x as of late 2025/early 2026
basic_information.license: Apache License 2.0 with additional conditions: commercial use allowed, but multi-tenant SaaS requires a separate commercial license from Dify; Dify branding/logo must not be removed from the console

technical_architecture.architecture_type: Microservices-oriented architecture deployed via Docker Compose or Kubernetes. Backend API layer (Flask/Python), frontend (React/TypeScript), Nginx reverse proxy, with support for horizontal scaling of workers. Containerized components enable elastic scaling. The Knowledge Pipeline was rebuilt around a queued graph execution model in 2025, allowing pipelines to start from any node, pause/resume, and support breakpoints and human-in-the-loop execution. Cloud-native design with TiDB consolidation reducing hundreds of thousands of database containers into a single unified system.
technical_architecture.language: Python (backend, Flask web framework), TypeScript/JavaScript (frontend, React with React Flow for visual workflow orchestration). Docker-based deployment with Nginx reverse proxy. REST API and SDKs for programmatic access.
technical_architecture.embedding_dimensions: Supports arbitrary embedding dimensions depending on the chosen embedding model. Compatible with all major embedding model outputs. Supports OpenAI text-embedding-3 series, Jina, Tongyi/Qwen, BGE, and any OpenAI-API-compatible embedding endpoint. Multimodal embedding models supported since v1.11.
technical_architecture.indexing_algorithm: Vector indexing via integrated vector database backends (Qdrant HNSW, Weaviate, Milvus, Chroma, pgvector, Elasticsearch kNN, TiDB Vector, Typesense, Oracle, Zilliz). Also supports keyword/BM25 indexing for sparse retrieval. Hybrid retrieval combines vector and keyword search with configurable top-k and optional reranking.
technical_architecture.scalability: Cloud-native deployment on Kubernetes with official Helm chart support (Enterprise edition). Horizontal scaling of workers behind Nginx gateway. TiDB integration for distributed storage at scale. Knowledge Pipeline serves 120+ countries. Enterprise edition supports multi-tenant management. The Higress AI Gateway can be used to address high-concurrency CPU bottlenecks with load balancing strategies reducing first-token latency by ~50%.
technical_architecture.deployment_options: Docker Compose (community self-hosted), Kubernetes with Helm charts (Enterprise edition), Dify Cloud (managed SaaS at dify.ai), AWS Marketplace, Microsoft Azure Marketplace, third-party managed hosting (Zeabur ~$7/month, Elest.io, Railway). Enterprise edition supports on-premise and private cloud deployments.

rag_specific_capabilities.retrieval_method: Supports three retrieval modes: dense vector search (cosine similarity), sparse keyword search (BM25), and hybrid retrieval combining both with configurable top-k. Optional reranking step after retrieval. Agentic RAG capability via Agent Node in workflows: iterative intent analysis, query rewriting, multi-source evidence evaluation, and fallback strategies for improved grounding and reliability.
rag_specific_capabilities.chunking_strategy_support: Two primary chunking modes: General Mode (fixed-size chunking with configurable chunk size and overlap) and Parent-Child Mode (hierarchical chunking). Chunking is currently primarily fixed-length based. Semantic chunking is a community-requested feature (GitHub Issue #19105) but not natively built-in as of early 2026. The Knowledge Pipeline (introduced 2025) enables visual orchestration of custom document processing pipelines with plugin-based extensibility for custom chunking strategies. Document-structure-aware parsing available through plugins.
rag_specific_capabilities.reranking_support: Built-in reranking support integrated into the retrieval pipeline. Compatible with reranking models from Cohere, Jina, and other providers via plugin ecosystem. Cross-encoder reranking available. Reranking can be enabled/disabled per knowledge base retrieval configuration. Score fusion for hybrid retrieval results.
rag_specific_capabilities.multimodal_support: Full multimodal knowledge base support since v1.11 (2025). Image vectorization and cross-modal retrieval: text-to-image, image-to-text, and image-to-image search. Supports JPG, PNG, GIF images (up to 2MB) via Markdown links. Multimodal embedding models (e.g., from AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Jina) can be selected for image vectorization. Workflows can process images, audio, and video. GPT-4 Vision and other multimodal LLMs supported for vision tasks. Plugin architecture supports multi-modal data processing tools.
rag_specific_capabilities.graph_rag_support: No built-in native GraphRAG engine. Graph-enhanced RAG available through third-party integration with InfraNodus, which uses its own GraphRAG implementation to extract main topics, key relationships, and blind spots from knowledge bases. InfraNodus can build knowledge graphs from data and export concepts/relations for prompt enhancement. Not as deeply integrated as RAGFlow's native GraphRAG. [uncertain]
rag_specific_capabilities.citation_grounding: Built-in citation attribution feature in the knowledge base. When enabled, LLM responses that cite knowledge base content display specific citation information below the response: original segment text, segment number, and matching degree score. Users can verify which chunks contributed to each answer. Agentic RAG workflows enable iterative evidence evaluation for improved grounding. Deep Research Workflow templates maintain Markdown citations and compile complete reference lists.
rag_specific_capabilities.context_window_optimization: Configurable top-k retrieval limits context to most relevant chunks. Reranking filters and prioritizes retrieved content before LLM generation. Knowledge Pipeline allows custom preprocessing to optimize chunk quality. Workflow nodes enable context compression and summarization strategies. Agent Node can iteratively refine queries and select evidence, reducing noise in context. No documented built-in automatic context compression or summarization specifically for window limits. [uncertain]

performance_and_benchmarks.latency: No official p50/p99 latency benchmarks published by Dify. Performance depends heavily on the chosen LLM provider, vector database backend, and deployment infrastructure. Higress AI Gateway integration can reduce first-token latency by ~50% through load balancing. In high-concurrency scenarios, CPU bottlenecks have been reported in production. Qdrant integration (Rust-based) delivers faster vector retrieval than some alternatives. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.throughput: No official QPS benchmarks published. Horizontal scaling via Kubernetes (Enterprise) allows increasing throughput by adding workers. Performance varies by LLM provider rate limits and vector database backend choice. TiDB integration enables handling large-scale concurrent database operations. Mid-sized e-commerce companies have reported handling 50K+ messages/month through Enterprise plan. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.accuracy_metrics: No published MTEB, BEIR, or standardized RAG benchmark scores for Dify as a platform. RAG accuracy depends on the chosen embedding model, chunking strategy, reranking model, and LLM. The Knowledge Pipeline's visual approach enables iterative quality improvement. Observability integrations (LangSmith, Langfuse) allow tracking accuracy metrics per deployment. [uncertain]
performance_and_benchmarks.benchmark_results: No standardized third-party benchmark results published for Dify as a complete RAG system. Empirical latency, accuracy, or reliability metrics have not been collected in recent third-party reviews. Performance characteristics are deployment-specific and depend on infrastructure choices. [uncertain]

integration_and_ecosystem.framework_compatibility: Dify operates as a self-contained AI application platform rather than a LangChain/LlamaIndex component. Notably, Dify removed LangChain from its codebase citing development speed constraints. Does not integrate as a native LangChain VectorStore or LlamaIndex plugin. Instead provides REST API, webhooks, and SDK for integration into existing application stacks. Plugin ecosystem enables extensible tool integration. Workflow engine supports custom integrations via HTTP request nodes and code execution nodes.
integration_and_ecosystem.model_compatibility: Extremely broad LLM provider support: OpenAI (GPT-4, GPT-4o, o1/o3 series), Anthropic (Claude 3/3.5/4 series), Google (Gemini), Mistral AI, DeepSeek (R1, V3), Qwen/Tongyi-Qianwen, Meta Llama, Cohere, and many more. Local model deployment via Ollama, Xinference, LocalAI, and vLLM. Open-source models via Hugging Face. Embedding models: OpenAI, Jina, Cohere, BGE, AWS Bedrock, Google Vertex AI, Tongyi. Any OpenAI-API-compatible endpoint supported. Model configuration via web UI Model Providers page.
integration_and_ecosystem.mcp_integration_status: Full built-in two-way MCP (Model Context Protocol) support since v1.6.0. Dify can call any external MCP server directly (HTTP-based, pre-authorized and auth-free modes) for accessing external APIs, databases, and services. Community-built MCP Server plugin turns any Dify app (Agent, Chatflow, Workflow) into an MCP-compliant server for external systems to consume. Enables integration with Claude, Cursor, and other MCP-compatible AI agents.
integration_and_ecosystem.data_source_connectors: Four primary data source types: file upload, online drive, online documents, and web crawler. Built-in connectors: Notion, Google Drive, Confluence, S3, Slack, GitHub (via webhooks/API). Web crawling integration with Firecrawl and Tavily for live web data ingestion. File upload supports: Word, PowerPoint, Excel, PDF, images, text files, Markdown, HTML. Knowledge Pipeline enables custom connectors from the Marketplace or standard interfaces for building custom connectors. Additional sources available via plugin ecosystem.
integration_and_ecosystem.observability_integration: Native integration with LangSmith and Langfuse (since v0.6.12). Enables comprehensive monitoring of accuracy, latency, cost, token usage, and resource utilization. Langfuse integration provides detailed tracing of RAG pipelines. LangSmith integration enables debugging and visualization of workflow execution. Arize integration documented for agent evaluation, monitoring, and improvement. Basic built-in resource usage statistics in Dify console. No documented native OpenTelemetry or Prometheus metrics export.

pricing_and_cost.pricing_model: Open-core model: open-source self-hosted (free, Apache 2.0 with conditions) plus managed cloud tiers. Cloud pricing: Sandbox (free), Professional ($59/workspace/month), Team ($159/workspace/month), Enterprise (custom pricing, contact sales). Self-hosted Community Edition is free. Enterprise self-hosted requires a commercial license for multi-tenant and branding customization.
pricing_and_cost.free_tier: Sandbox (Cloud): 200 message credits, 1 user, 5 apps, 50MB knowledge storage, no credit card required. Community Edition (self-hosted): fully free with all core features, unlimited usage, no feature gating on core capabilities. Self-hosted on Zeabur possible for ~$7/month infrastructure.
pricing_and_cost.cost_at_scale: Cloud Professional: $59/month for 3 team members, 5,000 message credits, 50 apps, 500 documents, 5GB knowledge storage. Cloud Team: $159/month for 50 team members, 10,000 message credits, 200 apps, 1,000 documents, 20GB storage. Cloud Enterprise: custom pricing for unlimited/higher limits. Self-hosted: $0 software + infrastructure costs (VM $30-200/month depending on scale). External LLM API costs are additional and usage-dependent. [uncertain]
pricing_and_cost.total_cost_of_ownership: Self-hosted Community: $0 licensing + $30-200/month infrastructure (VM, storage) + external LLM API costs ($0.50-15/1M tokens depending on provider) + embedding API costs + vector database costs (free if using built-in options like Weaviate/Qdrant). Cloud Professional: $59/month + LLM API costs (bring your own API keys). Enterprise: custom pricing includes dedicated support, SSO, multi-tenant management. Ops overhead for self-hosted: moderate (Docker Compose straightforward, Kubernetes requires Enterprise license). Staff time for maintenance and upgrades should be factored in. [uncertain]

adoption_and_market.market_position: Leader in the open-source AI application development platform space. One of the most starred open-source AI repositories globally (~129K GitHub stars). Positioned as the go-to low-code/no-code platform for building production-ready AI applications, differentiated from code-first frameworks like LangChain/LlamaIndex. Stronger in breadth (full-stack AI app platform) than depth (specialized RAG engine). Among the top 10 GitHub agentic AI repositories in 2025.
adoption_and_market.notable_customers: 30+ Fortune 500 companies across finance, manufacturing, retail, and healthcare. Enterprise customers span 120+ countries. Specific named customers not publicly disclosed. Use cases include: internal AI infrastructure hubs for governed AI access (banking sector), customer-facing chatbots handling 50K+ messages/month (e-commerce), and enterprise knowledge bases. Available on AWS Marketplace and Microsoft Azure Marketplace. Case study with AWS Lambda for scalable plugin platform. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.community_size: ~127K-129K GitHub stars (February 2026), making it one of the most popular open-source AI projects. 180,000+ developers in the community. 290+ community contributors (as of Q2 2024, likely higher now). 60,000+ developers using it for learning/experimentation. Active community forum at forum.dify.ai. Discord community present. X/Twitter: @dify_ai. Rapid growth: from 58K stars in January 2025 to 129K by February 2026.
adoption_and_market.funding_and_valuation: Total raised: $11.5M. Series A round in August 2024, led by AliCloud and Shenzhen Vcshare Fund Management. Other investors: 5Y Capital, Alibaba Cloud Computing, FutureX Capital, Beijing Delian Yuntong Investment Management, China Growth Capital. Revenue: $3.1M as of June 2025. ~70 employees globally. Specific valuation not publicly disclosed. Company registered as LangGenius Inc. [uncertain]
adoption_and_market.competitive_landscape: Direct competitors: Flowise (~30K stars, more developer-focused, basic logic control), Langflow (~42K stars in early 2025, acquired by DataStax, data-centric pipelines), RAGFlow (~73K stars, deeper document understanding but narrower scope), n8n (workflow automation with AI capabilities). Broader competitors: LangChain (code-first framework, more complex), LlamaIndex (data framework focus), Haystack (pipeline-as-code). Key differentiators: (1) most intuitive visual UI for non-technical users, (2) broadest LLM provider support, (3) full-stack platform (RAG + agents + workflows + LLMOps), (4) plugin marketplace ecosystem, (5) enterprise-grade with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001.

entrepreneurial_relevance.startup_applicability: Best for: teams of 1-50 building AI-powered applications quickly without deep ML engineering expertise. Ideal for startups that need to go from idea to production AI app in days rather than months. Team size: works for solo developers (Community/Professional) up to mid-size teams (Team/Enterprise). Budget: $0 self-hosted or $59-159/month cloud. Use case fit: customer-facing chatbots, internal knowledge bases, AI-powered SaaS features, content generation workflows, document Q&A, agentic automation. Particularly strong for: non-technical founders who need visual workflow builders, teams wanting to experiment with multiple LLM providers without code changes, and enterprises needing governed AI access with SSO/RBAC. Not recommended for: teams needing deep document parsing (RAGFlow better), teams building custom ML pipelines (LangChain/LlamaIndex better), or teams needing code-first flexibility with minimal abstraction.
entrepreneurial_relevance.build_vs_buy_guidance: Use Dify Cloud when: need fastest time-to-market, team lacks DevOps resources, acceptable to use shared infrastructure, budget allows $59-159/month. Self-host Dify when: need full data control, have Docker/K8s expertise, want to avoid per-seat costs at scale, need to comply with data residency requirements. Use Dify Enterprise when: need multi-tenant deployment, SSO (SAML/OIDC/OAuth2), SLA guarantees, and dedicated support. Consider alternatives when: need specialized deep document parsing (use RAGFlow), need maximum code-level control (use LangChain/LlamaIndex directly), or need a pure vector database solution (use Pinecone/Qdrant directly). Migration note: Dify is a full-stack platform, so migrating away requires rebuilding workflows, knowledge bases, and agent logic, not just swapping a component.
entrepreneurial_relevance.time_to_production: POC: 1-2 hours (sign up for Dify Cloud or docker compose up, configure LLM provider, create knowledge base, build simple chatbot). MVP with RAG: 1-3 days (upload documents, configure retrieval settings, build workflow, test via API). Production deployment: 1-4 weeks depending on complexity (workflow design, knowledge base optimization, API integration, security configuration, load testing). The visual workflow builder and no-code interface dramatically accelerate initial development. Enterprise deployments with SSO, multi-tenancy, and custom plugins may take 4-8 weeks.
key_lessons: 1. Start with Dify Cloud for validation, migrate to self-hosted for scale — The free Sandbox tier lets you validate your AI product idea in hours. Once product-market fit is confirmed, self-hosting eliminates per-seat costs and gives full data control. This two-phase approach minimizes both initial investment and long-term vendor lock-in.

2. The visual workflow builder is your secret weapon for stakeholder buy-in — Non-technical co-founders, investors, and enterprise buyers can see and understand the AI logic visually. Use Dify's workflow canvas in demos and pitches to make AI applications tangible and transparent, building trust faster than code-only approaches.

3. Dify's breadth is both its strength and limitation — As a full-stack platform covering RAG, agents, workflows, and LLMOps, Dify gets you to 80% quality fast. But for the last 20% (deep document parsing, custom retrieval algorithms, specialized evaluation), you may need to complement with specialized tools (RAGFlow for documents, LangSmith for advanced evaluation).

4. Plugin ecosystem reduces build-from-scratch costs — Instead of building custom integrations, check the Dify Marketplace first. Official and community plugins for tools, models, agent strategies, and data connectors can save weeks of development. Contribute plugins back to build community credibility.

5. Budget for LLM API costs separately from platform costs — Dify's pricing covers the platform, but LLM inference (your biggest variable cost) is billed separately through your own API keys. Model selection (GPT-4 vs Claude vs open-source via Ollama) dramatically impacts unit economics. Test with cheaper models first, upgrade only where quality demands it.
entrepreneurial_relevance.no_code_interface: Yes — Dify provides a comprehensive visual/no-code builder. Features include: drag-and-drop Workflow Studio for designing AI application logic, visual Knowledge Base management (upload, configure, preview), Agent builder with tool configuration, Chatflow and Workflow templates, prompt engineering playground, model provider configuration via UI, and one-click app deployment. The interface is designed to be accessible to non-technical users while offering enough depth for developers. Plugin installation and management also via visual Marketplace.
entrepreneurial_relevance.session_mapping: Session 2 (Prompt engineering & no-code tools — hands-on demo building a RAG chatbot with visual workflow builder, exploring prompt templates and knowledge base features), Session 3 (Framing & managing AI projects — Build vs Buy analysis using Dify as case study: when to use managed platform vs custom code, evaluating AI tools for enterprise deployment)

confidence.data_quality: High — information sourced from official Dify website (dify.ai), Dify blog posts, official documentation (docs.dify.ai), GitHub repository (langgenius/dify, 129K stars), Crunchbase, Tracxn, multiple independent review sites (Skywork, BayTech Consulting, GPTBots, AiX Society), AWS case study, and Dify's official X/Twitter announcements.
confidence.cross_reference: GitHub stars confirmed via GitHub (127K-129K range). Pricing tiers confirmed across multiple sources (dify.ai/pricing, G2, Elest.io, BayTech Consulting). Funding ($11.5M) confirmed via Crunchbase and Tracxn. SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certifications confirmed via official Dify X/Twitter announcement and docs. MCP support confirmed via official Dify blog (v1.6.0). Plugin ecosystem and v1.0 release confirmed via official blog and GitHub releases. Revenue ($3.1M) confirmed via GetLatka.
confidence.caveats: No official performance benchmarks published for Dify as a RAG system (latency, throughput, accuracy). Pricing tiers may change — confirm at dify.ai/pricing. The Apache 2.0 license has additional conditions (multi-tenant SaaS requires commercial license, branding restrictions) that are unusual and have sparked community debate. Specific enterprise customer names are not publicly disclosed. Revenue and employee counts are from mid-2025 and may have changed. The platform iterates rapidly (v1.0 to v1.11 within one year), which means features evolve quickly but API stability may be a concern. Chinese-language resources and community may be more comprehensive than English equivalents. GraphRAG is not natively built-in (available through third-party InfraNodus integration). Semantic chunking is community-requested but not yet natively implemented.
confidence.security_posture: Strong enterprise security posture: certified SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001:2022, and GDPR compliant. Enterprise edition supports SSO (SAML, OIDC, OAuth2), centralized access control, two-step verification, and MFA. Plugin system enforces rigorous code review, isolated execution with defined permissions, and explicit data handling declarations. Integrations with Palo Alto Networks (security engine for every model call) and Azure AI Content Safety (real-time content moderation). RAG-specific attack surfaces apply: knowledge base poisoning, prompt injection via retrieved content, embedding inversion. No documented HIPAA certification. Self-hosted deployments shift security responsibility to the deployer. Standard container security practices and network isolation recommended for production.
